summary: Esho Kawasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He was director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

Esho Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held an assistant professor post at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and served as professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
Esho Yamaguchi studied at Kyoto University and worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University (circa 1949–1968) and Osaka University as professor (attested 1980–1984).

Eshō Mikogami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū. He served as president of the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies in 1997, and was professor (until 2003) and professor emeritus (attested 2007–2010) at Ryukoku University.

Ester Bianchi earned her PhD circa 1999–2003 at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and EPHE under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna. Specializing in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she held posts at Florence (attested 2008) and Perugia (from circa 2007).

Etsuaki Teraishi specializes in Indology and philosophy. Posts held include assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Georg Bühler circa 1880–1882. From circa 1886 to 1903, he served as epigraphist for the Government of Madras, Archaeological Survey of India, and Government of India.

Eugen Pander worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (circa 1872–1876) and served as professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan in 1881.

Eugen Wilhelm specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under August Schleicher (circa 1860–1864) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1909. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1908–1913), Johns Hopkins University (circa 1914–1917), and Yale University (circa 1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield (circa 1992–1997), and held posts at the University of Chicago (circa 1996–1997) and Harvard University (from circa 1997).

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz studied at Lviv University (circa 1919–1925), where he also held a post (circa 1928–1939). In Indology and linguistics, he held later posts at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń and the University of Warsaw (circa 1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served at the Société Asiatique, as Inspecteur at the Imprimerie Nationale (circa 1832–1852), and as teacher at the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (circa 1828–1832) and Eugène Burnouf (circa 1832–1838).

Eugène Obermiller was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (circa 1921–1935). He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (circa 1927–1935) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (circa 1930–1935).

Eun-su Cho earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, she held an assistant professorship at the University of Michigan until 2004, then became professor at Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choi works in Buddhist studies. She obtained a doctorate from Korea University and held an HK professor post at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2015).

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2006, she was attested as Professor Emeritus at the University of Alberta and Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Rigzin. She held a post at the University of Calgary.

Evan Thompson studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto (PhD 1985–1990) under Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. His philosophy career includes posts at Concordia, York, the University of Toronto (2005), and the University of British Columbia (2013).
